steps.text: Out of the fridge: Sunday's chicken — take 105/140 g (245 g total) of the ~760 g roast batch — and Sunday's rice-and-cauliflower — rice 55/72 g dry (127 g total) of the 380 g dry batch, riced cauliflower 130/160 g (290 g total) of the ~810 g raw batch. 662 g all told.
The widest pan you own — or a wok — on high with the oil (7/9 g, rapeseed — it's hitting a hot wok). Onion (30/40 g) and pepper (70/90 g) diced, 3 minutes. You want colour on them, not softness.
Passata (80/100 g) with 1 tsp curry powder, ½ tsp thyme and a pinch of stock powder. Cook it down hard for 3 minutes, until it stops being loose.
Rice (55/72 g dry, cooked) and raw cauliflower (130/160 g) in. Press it flat and LEAVE it 60 seconds to catch before stirring. Then twice more.
Push everything to one side. Beaten egg (25 g) into the gap, scrambled fast, then folded through.
Chicken (105/140 g) in for the last minute. Spring onion (15/20 g) off the heat.

why: Leave the rice alone. Fried rice is made by contact with hot metal, not by stirring — every time you move it you drop the pan temperature and end up steaming it into porridge.
notes: D0-003: oil is a hot-wok cooking use throughout (frying onion, pepper, rice, chicken) — no dressing/finishing use in this dish, so the whole row renames olive_oil -> rapeseed_oil (7/9 g, unchanged grams).

Reviewer FIX 2 (cycle 1): batchTakeG convention unified to Week A's all-components sum (cf. a-d1l's 715 g = chicken+rice+cauliflower+white sauce). This card draws THREE Sunday components: chicken 105/140 g (245 g, of the 760 g roast batch, one of three consumers alongside b-d2l and b-d5l — 755 g taken in total, 5 g headroom, see prep-b.json), rice 55/72 g dry (127 g, of the 380 g dry batch) and riced cauliflower 130/160 g (290 g, of the ~810 g raw batch). Sum: 105+55+130=290 her, 140+72+160=372 him, 662 g total — restated in step 1 (chicken + rice + cauliflower named together) and again where each is actually used (rice+cauliflower in step 4, chicken in step 6).
Single wide-pan/wok flow — genuinely sequential, no parallel track markup needed.
No macro drift beyond the oil relabel (identical per100g to olive_oil, zero kcal change).
